title: React Server Components with AI Data Fetching
description: Leverage React Server Components (RSC) to pre-fetch AI data, stream partial UI, and optimize server-side rendering for AI-powered pages.

data.text: React Server Components: Server-First AI Rendering

React Server Components render on the server and stream HTML to the client. Unlike client components, they don't ship JavaScript bundles to the browser. For AI applications, this means you can fetch LLM data server-side, render the initial response immediately, and progressively enhance with interactive client components only where needed — dramatically reducing bundle size and Time to First Byte.

data.caption: RSC rendering flow for AI-powered pages
data.definition:
flowchart LR
    ClientReq[Client Request] --> ServerComp["Server Component\n(Async Data Fetch)"]
    ServerComp --> AsyncAwait{await AI\nResponse?}
    AsyncAwait -->|Streaming| StreamResp[Stream Partial UI]
    AsyncAwait -->|Resolved| FullRender[Full Render]
    StreamResp --> ClientHydration["Client Hydration\n(Client Components Only)"]
    FullRender --> ClientHydration
    ClientHydration --> Interactive[Interactive AI UI]
    ServerComp -->|Server Actions| BackendAPI[.NET Backend API]

data.text: In React Server Components, you can use async/await directly in the component body. This is perfect for fetching AI data from your .NET backend — the component suspends until data is ready, and React streams the rendered output incrementally to the client.

data.text: Server Components support React Suspense for streaming. While slow data (like an LLM summary) is fetching, the user sees the rest of the page immediately. Once the summary resolves, it streams in and the user sees it appear without a full page reload.

data.text: Server Components cannot use useState or other client-side hooks. Any interactive element that needs state management must be a separate client component, imported and used within the server component. This separation is automatic and enforced by Next.js 15.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Server Components run on the server, reducing client bundle size for AI-heavy pages
Async/await in component bodies suspends rendering until data resolves
Suspense streams partial UI while awaiting slow operations
Separate interactive elements into client components with 'use client'
Perfect for pre-fetching LLM-generated content server-side
data.takeaway: RSC enables server-first AI rendering: heavy data fetching and AI inference happen server-side, streaming progressive UI to the client with minimal JavaScript.
